# Factory Real-Host Assurance

Use an authorized, disposable product engagement to test the framework's actual
behavior, not just its definitions. Follow [artifact ownership and contracts](../artifact-storage-and-engagement-contracts/SKILL.md),
[Factory recovery](../factory-mvp-and-recovery/SKILL.md), and
[empirical Done](../fullstack-empirical-done/SKILL.md). This method grants no
permission, future cycles, fault injection, installation, or scheduler authority.

## Declare the experiment

1. Retrieve product storage guidance and reuse one accepted contract. Record
   the human's authorized outcome, trial count/horizon, exclusions, participants,
   write ownership, data isolation, fault scope, cleanup, and restart route.
   Clarify genuinely missing scope; do not add another tool-authorization gate.
2. Freeze the criteria before execution. Separate a new implementation,
   reproduction of an existing artifact, independent verification, attended
   recovery, and customer-value realization. Rebuilding a copy or repeating a
   test suite is not an independently created product or a value cycle.
3. Record the actual session/harness, OS, runtime, tool/browser versions, source
   manifest, package/lockfile identity, and entrypoint. Distinguish a full source
   tree from a selected input manifest and fingerprint added assurance code
   separately. Keep excluded secrets and local data out of evidence.

Bind the accepted operating profile and its source/contract revision to the
trial. Record cost, latency and human intervention alongside outcome quality,
using current model/tool availability, quotas and sourced prices. Compare with
the agreed simpler baseline inside the approved budget/horizon. A bounded
return, a parallel overlap observation and supervised restart are different
claims; do not substitute one for another or relabel a failed profile.

## Exercise the live system

4. Start with shipped capability diagnostics, then make harmless in-scope live
   calls before depending on a capability. A setting, loaded tool, agent
   definition, or successful standalone hook test is not a live observation.
   Record actual accepted roles, agent IDs, and parent/nested tool calls for
   the required hierarchy. Do not invent unavailable members or independence.
   Compare the actual execution interface at each depth, not just declared
   tool aliases. A working parent does not prove a working descendant.
   Check whether invocations are one-shot before designing handshakes: give a
   one-shot agent the complete initial assignment and predeclared acceptance
   event; do not rely on a later `ACTIVATE` message. If an interface is missing,
   preserve the failure and obtain required owner approval before changing
   protected agent tool surfaces or substituting an executor.
5. Observe host grants and prompt counts separately from task acceptance.
   Unknown counts remain unknown. Classify a missing executable, missing tool,
   timeout, test-harness defect, product defect, and host denial distinctly.
   Recover a capability failure using an already-authorized available route
   only when no denial applies. Never retry or route around a denied action
   without independently changed authority/capability evidence.
   Collect operator-observed confirmation counts when host telemetry is
   unavailable, preserving exact responses and uncertainty. Separate initial
   grant warnings, routine subagent read/edit prompts, scope decisions, app
   dialogs and authentication. Repeated routine prompts despite a selected
   broad session mode are an approval-configuration incident and a failed
   autonomy gate, even if all product trials pass. Do not suppress the host.
   Inspect reference/product workspace roots and host path boundaries as
   separate capabilities; distinct artifact ownership does not grant filesystem
   access. Preserve unverified cause hypotheses as such, and never relocate
   product work into the framework merely to avoid approval prompts.
6. Produce an isolated runnable artifact using the recorded recipe and approved
   dependencies. Do not silently share mutable state or dependency directories
   while calling a run clean or independent. Record the artifact actually run;
   an alternative test wrapper does not verify the original entrypoint.
7. Verify the required behavior through its real surface. Unit/API/SDK tests do
   not replace browser or installed simulator criteria. For responsive checks,
   assert the **observed** CSS viewport equals the requested width at the tested
   states and `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`; include real scrollbar space and
   long content. Editor resizing, hidden tabs, and screenshots can change the
   effective viewport. Genuine browser device/focus emulation is acceptable
   when disclosed; overriding DOM metrics or force-clicking obstructed controls
   is not proof. Requery controls after a render changes their accessible name.
   Exercise keyboard operation and native internal focus stops; distinguish
   computed outline/tree evidence from screen-reader or compliance claims.
   A successful interception API call or injected header is not enforcement
   proof: exercise the affected redirect, worker, frame, popup, beacon and
   WebSocket paths against owned negative fixtures and check actual destination
   counters. Keep failed guards failed. A supported server-only simulator path
   may satisfy only criteria that allow that surface; never relabel it GUI
   evidence or silently relax locality.
8. Have the assigned verifier inspect primary artifacts/results rather than
   accept the producer's summary. Retain failed attempts, changed hypotheses,
   exact commands/tool parameters, timestamps, expected/observed results, source
   and evidence digests, and access status. Fix only evidenced in-scope defects;
   a source change invalidates affected observations and reproduced artifacts.

## Recover and reconcile

9. Inject only the approved fault into an explicitly owned isolated runtime.
   Before interruption, record its PID/identity, listeners, durable checkpoint,
   state digest, accepted work, and pending decisions. Observe the interruption,
   restart via the saved recipe under current authority, then verify preserved
   state, integration behavior, and no unintended replay. For confirmation-gated
   agents, test stale, consumed, cancelled, and pending proposals across restart.
   Process recovery is not Factory-session or unattended-supervisor recovery.
10. Use the required recovery panel for a material impasse. Keep independent
    authorized work moving without hiding a failed prerequisite, widening WIP,
    inventing demand, or manufacturing approval. With no supervisor, identify
    the actual human/runtime resume route instead of promising continuity.
11. Reconcile every trial and mandatory criterion as `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`,
    `NOT RUN`, or justified `NOT APPLICABLE`. Bind each result to its evaluated
    identity and evidence class. Keep operational trial counts, value-cycle
    counts, host-permission results, and user outcomes separate. A finite
    passing sample supports only the observed bounded result, not universal
    reliability, production readiness, or an unmeasured score.
12. Stop only engagement-owned helpers, verify their exact processes/listeners
    exited, preserve required artifacts, and remove only named temporary data.
    Submit the evidence matrix to Kanban; unresolved mandatory gates stay on
    the unfinished board. Record human acceptance and release separately.

## Required proof packet

- Contract, source/input and assurance-code identities, environment, and recipe.
- Actual role acceptances/hierarchy, host observations, and unobservable fields.
- Trial-by-criterion matrix with primary evidence and residual limitations.
- Failure/recovery ledger, fault/checkpoint/state/replay observations, cleanup.
- Honest bounded verdict, missing decisions, and a dispatchable restart route.

Store that packet in the product workspace, never in this skill directory.
